name: USAir red and maroon on bare metal (1985)
description: USAir's scheme from the 1979 rename until the 1989 gray scheme, as worn in 1985: a polished bare metal aircraft with one band along it just under the windows, edged above and below by thin white pinstripes. The band is red from the nose to a line leaning aft just ahead of the wing, and maroon from there to the tail. Behind the last windows the upper body turns red along a line parallel to the fin's leading edge, so the tail and fin are red, with a bare metal band along the fin's leading edge and, on the DC-9 and 737, a maroon band toward the trailing edge parallel to it. 'USAIR' in heavy extended capitals over the forward windows, 'US' red and 'AIR' maroon, and in white across the fin. A small US flag ahead of the registration over the aft windows. Bare metal wings; maroon nacelles on the DC-9 and the 727's side engines, bare metal on the 737.

sources.title: US Airways, Wikipedia
sources.note: History: Allegheny renamed USAir on 28 October 1979; US Airways from 1997; merged into American, whose last US Airways flight (US 1939) landed on 17 October 2015. The 1989 scheme replaced this one after the Piedmont merger.

notes: Measured 2026-11-26 for ghost flights (USAir's February 1985 Pittsburgh schedule) on DC-9-31 N921VJ (December 1986, the sharpest dated photo) on shapes/DC93.json, checked on DC-9-31s of 1983, 1984 and March 1985; the 737-200 (N328AU, 1984 and 1988) and the 727-200 (N755US, 1989, checked on 1984-85 photos) measured as types. One scheme: every dated photo from 1980 to early 1989 of the DC-9-30, 737-200 and 727-200 shows it, and the BAC One-Elevens wore it too (not drawn: no shape). Second-hand aircraft kept their old paint for a while after the 1987-89 PSA and Piedmont mergers, which is after 1985. Every band edge is a level line in meters from the nose to the tail, and the split and the tail's sweep are straight lines (the sweep's real edge curves a little near the band). The pinstripes are about 4 cm. The fin title is lettered in a close font; the real wordmark's A is a peak without a crossbar and its U and S are wide and rounded. Colors are readings off slides and the public-domain logo, not USAir's specification. The registration (black, aft of the flag) isn't drawn.

B722.note: 727-200 N755US (February 1989), checked on the 1984-85 photos: the band from 0.24 m to -0.60 m with white pinstripes, just under the windows (0.39-0.73 m); the split about 1.4 m ahead of the first overwing exit, harder to place on the 727 (the shade changes gently in the photos). The fin's metal leading-edge band is wider (2.1 m, over the S-duct's fairing) and no maroon band shows on the 727's fin; the red's front edge runs down parallel to it to the band at about 32.5 m (the photo's edge curves in near the band, nearer 33 m). Maroon side nacelles with metal lips. Title capitals 0.71 m, 5.3 m long from 8.0 m; the fin's title low, its baseline at the fin's root over the fairing.

B733.note: 737-200 N328AU (June 1984 side-on, September 1988 close): the band from 0.20 m to -0.37 m with white pinstripes either side, its top pinstripe touching the windows' bottoms (0.25 m); the split 1.0 m ahead of the overwing exit, leaning aft 0.45 m. The red's front edge on the tail 0.95 m behind the fin's leading edge, meeting the band just ahead of the aft door; the maroon on the fin 2.75 m behind the leading edge, a narrow band at the tip widening to the root. Bare metal nacelles. Title capitals 0.50 m, 3.85 m long from 5.6 m. Drawn on the 737-300 shape, the repo's stand-in for the -200 (a longer body and the -300's engines).
